effect-smol.purpose: Read-only Effect v4 source pinned to the tag matching the effect catalog — the authority on what v4 actually exports, plus the v3→v4 migration notes.

effect.purpose: Read-only Effect v4 source pinned to the tag matching the effect catalog — the authority on what v4 actually exports, plus the v3→v4 migration notes and the @effect/vitest reference implementation. Tracks the main Effect-TS/effect monorepo (v4 development moved back there on 2026-07-19 when the effect-smol repo was archived); vendored at .repos/effect since the 2026-07-24 rename, matching the path a consuming repo would use.

orientation.layout: Sparse checkout: packages/effect (core source + package.json exports map), packages/vitest (@effect/vitest reference implementation), migration/ (per-domain v3→v4 notes), ai-docs/, LLMS.md, MIGRATION.md.
orientation.startHere: packages/effect/src settles what v4 actually exports (evidence-ladder rung 2); migration/*.md settles v3→v4 renames (rung 1). Before trusting an answer, check the pin matches the installed effect version — node_modules wins on disagreement.

effected.purpose: Read-only source for the @effected package kit (25 Effect v4 packages: github-actions, github, commands, npm, sbom, format parsers, workspace/git introspection, and more), pinned to main HEAD rather than a release tag because the kit is actively dogfooded and this repo consumes in-progress APIs. The authority on what each package actually exports and how its services and test doubles are shaped — read it before re-implementing a capability the kit already ships.

orientation.layout: pnpm monorepo, one directory per published package under packages/<name>/ with src/, test files co-located, and its own CLAUDE.md. design/ holds the kit's internal design docs. The website/, lib/, plugin/ and lockfile trees are excluded from the sparse checkout.
orientation.startHere: packages/<name>/src/index.ts for a package's real export surface, and its CLAUDE.md for the intended usage. Pinned to main HEAD, not a release tag — the checkout may be ahead of any published version, so node_modules settles what this repo can actually call today.
